notes: The brownstone at Sixth Avenue and St. Johns Place filmed as the family house that Joan keeps after the split; the film names no street for it. Baumbach told IndieWire it belonged to his childhood friend Ben and his wife Molly and was also used for interiors. It sold for $3.45 million in 2012 (The Real Deal) and survives.

household: with Walt and Frank on alternating days; his student Lili later takes his extra room
creator: Noah Baumbach
address_as_given: an elegant new house across the park; the street's Stratford Road
geocode_query: Stratford Road and Beverley Road, Brooklyn
notes: Bernard calls it an elegant new house across Prospect Park, five subway stops away; Walt later says the street is Stratford Road, with no house number. Stratford Road runs about 1.5 km through Prospect Park South and Ditmas Park, so the point is its midpoint. A 2005 Park Slope blog review placed the house in Ditmas Park. Baumbach's father, Jonathan Baumbach, later owned a Victorian at 208 Marlborough Road in Prospect Park South, a few blocks away (6sqft, 2015, which does not say when he bought it); Baumbach himself grew up on Montgomery Place in Park Slope (Bedford + Bowery). Context only.
source_quote: The street's Stratford Road. My dad's moving there. I hear it's the fillet of the neighborhood.
source2_quote: I've got an elegant new house across the park.
